name: Web experiences
short: A clear first impression. A useful next step.
description: Business websites with clear positioning, accessible interfaces and a focused path from discovery to inquiry.
problem: Visitors arrive, but struggle to understand your offer or take the next step.
approach: Start with the buyer’s questions, map the information they need, and build a fast website around the actions that matter.
deliverables: Responsive design system and reusable pages
Search metadata, structured data and launch checks
inputs: Your current website, services, audience, brand assets and the actions you want visitors to take.
measure: Qualified inquiries, form completion and the speed of key landing pages.
boundary: Copywriting volume, translations, integrations and ongoing maintenance are agreed in the scope.

name: Business software
short: Less spreadsheet juggling. More shared context.
description: Custom internal tools that connect records, permissions and everyday work in one understandable workflow.
problem: Important work moves between spreadsheets, messages and people who hold the missing context.
approach: Map one complete workflow before building. Define the record of truth, who can change it, and how mistakes are corrected.
deliverables: Core records, validation and audit requirements
Import, backup and operational handover plan
inputs: A sample of your current workflow with fictional data, team roles, recurring exceptions and existing tools.
measure: Time to complete a task, duplicate entry and unresolved handoffs.
boundary: Security, retention and migration requirements are assessed before real business data is introduced.

name: AI & automation
short: Automate the repeatable. Keep people in control.
description: Practical AI assistants and workflow automation with clear limits, approved knowledge and human review.
problem: Your team repeatedly classifies requests, answers the same questions or transfers information by hand.
approach: Separate deterministic steps from tasks that benefit from a model. Add approvals where a wrong answer or action would be costly.
deliverables: Evaluation examples, limits and failure handling
inputs: Representative tasks, approved reference material, the systems involved and examples of unacceptable outcomes.
measure: Useful resolutions, review time, correction rate and cost per completed task.
boundary: Model usage and external providers have separate running costs. A prototype is evaluated before automation expands.

name: Operational dashboards
description: Dashboards that turn business records into clear priorities, useful filters and actionable reporting.
problem: Your team has data, but finding the next action means opening several reports.
approach: Define each metric, its source and the decision it supports. Make exceptions visible before adding decorative charts.
deliverables: Date filters, empty states and export workflows
inputs: Sample data, metric definitions, reporting frequency and the decisions each role needs to make.
measure: Time to find an exception, reporting effort and agreement with the source records.
boundary: A dashboard cannot correct unreliable source data automatically. Data quality work is scoped explicitly.

name: Commerce experiences
short: A considered journey from browse to basket.
description: Product and ordering experiences with clear availability, reliable totals and a practical operations handoff.
problem: Customers cannot easily find an item, understand the total or complete an order confidently.
approach: Make catalog structure, stock rules and checkout responsibilities explicit. Review the operator’s workflow as carefully as the storefront.
inputs: Catalog data, stock rules, delivery areas, payment requirements and your current commerce platform.
measure: Basket completion, order corrections and stock reconciliation.
boundary: Payment accounts, refunds, tax and fulfillment rules need business approval. Demo orders never move real money.

name: Search & AI visibility
short: Make your expertise easier to discover.
description: Technical SEO, clear service content and trustworthy entity information for search and AI-assisted discovery.
problem: People cannot find your business, or the pages they find do not answer their questions.
approach: Check crawlability and intent first. Improve the service pages, evidence, internal links and structured information that help people evaluate you.
deliverables: Unique metadata and truthful structured data
inputs: Your domain, Search Console access, target audiences, services and evidence you can publish.
measure: Relevant impressions, qualified organic visits and inquiries over time.
boundary: Rankings, AI citations and indexing are controlled by external platforms. No position or inclusion is guaranteed.
